content:
Prince Harry is reportedly considering making a documentary about his late mother, Princess Diana, according to People magazine on Monday.

Multiple sources told the outlet that "Harry has also reached out to family members and friends connected to his late mother," but they stressed that "no documentary project has been finalised or confirmed."

The report comes as the 30th anniversary of Princess Diana's death approaches.

The Princess of Wales was just 36 years old when she died in a high-speed car crash in Paris on 31 August 1997, after being pursued by paparazzi. Prince William was 15 and Prince Harry was only 12 at the time.

A source close to the Duke of Sussex told HuffPost that the royal "has discussed several potential projects" to mark the significant anniversary and "is still considering the best way to honour her legacy."

Speculation that he would produce a project about his mother has long been expected, ever since his and Meghan Markle's deal with Netflix was first announced in 2020.

HuffPost has reached out to representatives for Prince Harry as well as Kensington Palace; both declined to comment.

Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, previously announced he would publish a new book to mark 30 years since his beloved sister's death.

The new book, titled "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," is set for release on 22 September.

Spencer said in a press release announcing the new book: "As the 30th anniversary of Diana's tragic death approaches, I find myself once again being asked to give interviews about my sister."

He said: "This has prompted me to finally put my thoughts and memories into writing, so that I will no longer have to wade through others' commentaries, many of which are built on falsehoods that have become accepted as truth over the years."

The historian added: "The purpose of writing this book is precisely to tell Diana's true story from her brother's perspective, much like my attempt at her funeral. As with that eulogy, I hope to speak for Diana in an honest and positive way."
